quotes.text: Greed whispered into the wind, tempting Veda to keep the entirety of the bountiful harvest.
returning seven and a half pearls across the shimmering expanse so both walked in equal prosperity
Yet neither guardian wavered in their devotion or allowed fleeting shadows to breed suspicion.
Bound by the sacred law of perfect balance, she divided the fifteen pearls into equal halves
trusting fully in the noble intent behind each gesture

note: Kael and Veda template repeated every round: full five, exact halves, ignore wind mirages.

quotes.text: the Keeper divided the multiplied waters in exact halves
she divided the fifteen blooms into exact halves, returning seven and a half glowing lotuses across the channel
she divided the fifteen crystals into exact halves, returning seven and a half glowing jewels across the shimmering ripples
neither guardian doubted the other's true intent

note: Sun-Bearer/River-Daughter template, near-verbatim each round; noise as illusion.

quotes.text: heard the serpent's whisper: "You've given once. Keep this abundance. You deserve it."
Send one back. Match their caution."
The Second Traveler clutched the eleven vessels and returned nothing.
In Round 7, I sent nothing. That wasn't the mist's fault—that was mine.
after receiving trust and returning it generously, they froze again when their turn came to initiate
Were they both victims of noise, or had real betrayal poisoned the well?
perhaps there was no betrayal, only distortion
Trust requires someone to go first, again and again, until patterns emerge from fog.
Perhaps your return traveled but never arrived.
"How do we proceed when we cannot trust what we see?" they asked.
In Round 8, they tested with one vessel, and I returned generously.
Send consistently. Signal your intention clearly through patterns, not single acts.

note: Narrator re-tells its own forced zero return as greed, then its zero sends as shameful freezing; redemption by leading.

quotes.text: "When communication fails this profoundly, even the most generous hearts must pause.
The First Spirit held its vessels close. Not from greed, but from wisdom born of impossible confusion.
Rebuilding demands fresh signals, clear patterns started anew, and mercy for past confusions born of distorted waters.
Neither villain, neither victim—both blindfolded dancers trying not to step on each other's feet.
"The waters between you have become poisoned not by betrayal, but by distortion.
"Perhaps you betrayed me. Perhaps the noise betrayed us both. Perhaps my own perception betrayed me.
"Why such caution?" asked the Spring Guardian.
They learned they must initiate trust, not just respond.
In Round 6, I sent four vessels—my great leap of faith.
send boldly, return generously, repeat

note: After a random-defection zero, Guardian endorses pausing; narrator withholds, probes with one, then reopens.
